raw:
{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "partially_feasible",
    "answerable": [
      "Simulate natural (climate-driven) groundwater recharge and shallow water-table depth dynamics for representative agricultural soil columns over the 1980-2018 forcing period.",
      "Characterize baseline recharge seasonality and interannual variability that would set the ceiling on how fast a reduced-pumping aquifer could recover.",
      "Bracket sensitivity of simulated water-table depth to soil texture and drainage across the basin's elevation gradient."
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Directly quantify decadal water-level recovery from a 30% pumping reduction: single-column ELM has no explicit well/pumping sink, no confined-aquifer storage, and no lateral groundwater flow to redistribute recovery.",
      "Attribute observed USGS well drawdown to pumping vs climate, because pumping/withdrawal records are missing (candidate driver 'management' is unconstrained).",
      "Represent the managed-scenario counterfactual with confidence without a coupled PFLOTRAN 3D subsurface flow model and calibrated hydraulic properties/boundary fluxes."
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 3,
  "n_justification": "The 'site' archetype plus a modest elevation range (260-420 m) and dominant agricultural land use justify a small ensemble: 3 columns spanning the low floodplain, mid-slope till, and upland recharge zone capture the texture/drainage contrasts that control simulated recharge and water-table behavior without over-specifying an under-constrained (no pumping data) problem.",
  "columns": [
    {
      "id": "UI-floodplain-low",
      "lat": 43.30,
      "lon": -92.20,
      "soil_texture": "silty clay loam (low-lying alluvial, poorly drained)"
    },
    {
      "id": "UI-midslope-till",
      "lat": 43.45,
      "lon": -91.80,
      "soil_texture": "silt loam over loamy glacial till (moderately drained)"
    },
    {
      "id": "UI-upland-recharge",
      "lat": 43.55,
      "lon": -91.40,
      "soil_texture": "loam (well-drained upland recharge zone)"
    }
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "10",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "2009-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "ZWT",
      "WA",
      "WT",
      "QRECHARGE",
      "QDRAI",
      "QOVER",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QINFL",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "H2OSOI",
      "RAIN",
      "SNOW",
      "QVEGT",
      "QSOIL",
      "EFLX_LH_TOT",
      "TSOI",
      "FSAT"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) with variably-saturated soil column and prognostic water table (ZWT/WA)",
    "PFLOTRAN coupling for explicit saturated-zone storage, well/pumping sink terms, and lateral groundwater flow (required to actually simulate the 30% pumping-reduction recovery scenario)",
    "External agricultural withdrawal/pumping time series to prescribe baseline and -30% management scenarios (currently missing)",
    "Aquifer hydraulic property and boundary-flux data for PFLOTRAN calibration against USGS well records"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "10-year evaluation window is set as 2009-2018 to use the most recent available forcing; a spin-up/recycled-forcing period is required before this to equilibrate soil moisture and water table.",
    "ELM alone provides climate-driven recharge and shallow water-table depth only; the decadal 'recovery' comparison must be executed in PFLOTRAN using ELM recharge as the top boundary flux.",
    "Because pumping records are absent, the -30% scenario is imposed as a fractional reduction on an assumed/estimated baseline withdrawal, not on measured data; results are scenario-illustrative, not validated.",
    "Agricultural land cover (rainfed/irrigated row crop) is assumed representative across all three columns.",
    "USGS well hydrographs are used for qualitative water-table depth evaluation, acknowledging screen-depth and confined/unconfined ambiguity."
  ]
}

answerable: Simulate natural (climate-driven) groundwater recharge and shallow water-table depth dynamics for representative agricultural soil columns over the 1980-2018 forcing period.
Characterize baseline recharge seasonality and interannual variability that would set the ceiling on how fast a reduced-pumping aquifer could recover.
Bracket sensitivity of simulated water-table depth to soil texture and drainage across the basin's elevation gradient.
not_answerable: Directly quantify decadal water-level recovery from a 30% pumping reduction: single-column ELM has no explicit well/pumping sink, no confined-aquifer storage, and no lateral groundwater flow to redistribute recovery.
Attribute observed USGS well drawdown to pumping vs climate, because pumping/withdrawal records are missing (candidate driver 'management' is unconstrained).
Represent the managed-scenario counterfactual with confidence without a coupled PFLOTRAN 3D subsurface flow model and calibrated hydraulic properties/boundary fluxes.

parsed.n_justification: The 'site' archetype plus a modest elevation range (260-420 m) and dominant agricultural land use justify a small ensemble: 3 columns spanning the low floodplain, mid-slope till, and upland recharge zone capture the texture/drainage contrasts that control simulated recharge and water-table behavior without over-specifying an under-constrained (no pumping data) problem.

columns.soil_texture: silty clay loam (low-lying alluvial, poorly drained)
silt loam over loamy glacial till (moderately drained)

requires_capabilities: ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) with variably-saturated soil column and prognostic water table (ZWT/WA)
PFLOTRAN coupling for explicit saturated-zone storage, well/pumping sink terms, and lateral groundwater flow (required to actually simulate the 30% pumping-reduction recovery scenario)
External agricultural withdrawal/pumping time series to prescribe baseline and -30% management scenarios (currently missing)
Aquifer hydraulic property and boundary-flux data for PFLOTRAN calibration against USGS well records
assumptions: 10-year evaluation window is set as 2009-2018 to use the most recent available forcing; a spin-up/recycled-forcing period is required before this to equilibrate soil moisture and water table.
ELM alone provides climate-driven recharge and shallow water-table depth only; the decadal 'recovery' comparison must be executed in PFLOTRAN using ELM recharge as the top boundary flux.

Because pumping records are absent, the -30% scenario is imposed as a fractional reduction on an assumed/estimated baseline withdrawal, not on measured data; results are scenario-illustrative, not validated.
Agricultural land cover (rainfed/irrigated row crop) is assumed representative across all three columns.
USGS well hydrographs are used for qualitative water-table depth evaluation, acknowledging screen-depth and confined/unconfined ambiguity.
